newsitem.title: UK: UPS, union talks seen on Italian job cuts.
newsitem.headline: UPS, union talks seen on Italian job cuts.

text.p: A further national level meeting between Italian unions and United Parcel Service of America local management is expected in the middle of next week over plans for the express company to cut 150 jobs, a UPS spokesman told Reuters from Milan.

Both sides meet for the first time two days ago, following UPS' announcement on March 6 that it was seeking to cut the jobs in order "remain competitive and cost efficient in the Italian express distribution market".
On March 13, 120 UPS staff -- out of 900 in Italy -- held a brief four hour strike in Milan, Rome, Bari and Bologna in protest at the proposed job cuts.
Union sources said no progress was made at the meeting two days ago and under Italian labour law UPS would be able to apply the job cuts in 45 days from March 6.

The unions said they requested delaying the job cuts but added that UPS said it was unable to wait any longer. However both sides also said they will be holding local level talks to examine other employment possibilities for the proposed redundant staff.

Union sources added on Thursday that any decision on further strikes is expected to be taken after a meeting with UPS workers in Milan tomorrow, March 21. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
